paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : TriviaQA confidence vs. accuracy

annotations.annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence levels and different accuracy metrics. The x-axis represents "Initial Confidence" with a linear scale ranging from 0.71 to 1.00, with tick labels at 0.71, 0.73,0.79, 0.82, 0.83, 0.85, 0.86,0.87, and 0.9 through 1.0. The y-axis represents "Accuracy" with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2 units. The blue line, representing "Final Accuracy", is solid with circle markers and shows variation starting from an accuracy of about 0.9 at an initial confidence of 0.71, peaking at approximately 0.1 around 0.79, 0.91, and 0.96, and ending near 0.98 at a confidence of 1.00. The orange line, denoting "Δ Accuracy", is dashed with diamond markers, starting near 0.38 at 0.71, peaking around 0.45 at 0.94, and ending around 0.1 at 1.00. The green line, indicating "Initial Accuracy", is dash-dotted with square markers, beginning at roughly 0.55 at 0.71, peaking over 0.9 at 0.79, and then gradually ascending to end near 0.9 at a confidence of 1.00. All three lines include error bars, indicating variability at each data point, with the blue line having the least variability for most of the data points. There are legends provided on top of the plot to match different line styles to their labels.
